newsitem.title: UK: Pechiney president urges LME transparency.
newsitem.headline: Pechiney president urges LME transparency.

text.p: Pechiney SA president Jean-Pierre Rodier said on Tuesday that the Sumitomo scandal demonstrated that more transparency in the metals market was needed and it was a reform that would not cost a lot of money.

"What is at stake here is the health of the market," the head of the major French aluminium group said in the keynote speech at the annual dinner of the London Metal Exchange (LME). He said there were many improvements that the LME could make and one that would not involve much cost was transparency.
The Pechiney group incorporates LME ring trader Brandeis.
Rodier in his speech outlined several steps that he said might follow a top-to-bottom review of London-based metals trading begun by the Securities and Investment Board (SIB).

The SIB, the top British markets regulator, opened the inquiry in the aftermath of alleged rogue trading at Sumitomo Corp that is said to have cost the Japanese firm $2.6 billion and built up a huge long position.
"I support the LME chairman (Raj Bagri) who has warned of over-regulation...but there will be over-regulation if there is another event like Sumitomo," Rodier said.
Rodier recalled that the SIB had sent a letter to participants in the industry posing 33 open questions about the market.
"The aim is to get markets that are transparent where everybody is treated fairly," he said.
Rodier also noted that 45 percent of Pechiney profits were affected by price volatility, so the company becomes nervous when what he said were irresponsible players were involved in the market.
"Some actors have abused the marketplace -- they may provide liquidity but they have to abide by the rules," he said.
He said one measure that should be implemented was to limit the influence of over-the-counter instruments by bringing them on to the exchange. This has happened with average rate options.
LME rules could also be changed to establish what he called the trackability of stocks, while steps should be taken to provide early warning of undesirable situations developing in the market.
Non-cash clearing should be retained but more control put on credit lines, with some clients requiring their individual companies' board approval.
Stock financing activity similarly needed looking at, while a better balance was needed on the LME board so that all areas of the metal industry were represented.
